title: An image becomes context for an answer
subtitle: Put the sixteen patch rows of the tabletop scene in front of a question, let one attention block read them, and follow the answer word by word: what it reads, why it says two, and where it goes wrong.
audience: Students who completed the attention series and Vision I to III
centralLabel: The image is context; the answer is the next token

legendTitle: The seven objects, now over sixteen image rows and a few words
provenance: Scope: the image encoder is Vision I's frozen worksheet, applied to the same 8×8 scene; a 4×3 connector and a width-three one-head decoder with a ten-word vocabulary were fitted on scenes A and B only, then rounded to two decimals, and every number on this page is recomputed from those parameters in the browser. Scene C is a probe the model never saw. This is not a pretrained VLM and not a general counter; the toy has no LayerNorm, feed-forward sublayer or dropout.

footer: Image-conditioned generation still predicts one token at a time; the image is context, exactly like the earlier words.
hook: How many mugs? Four words and a picture. How does an image become context for an answer that is written one token at a time?
